analysis.title: Mutual Fundamentals: Mutual funds remain selective within the AI complex
key_insights: 42% of large-cap active mutual funds are beating their benchmarks YTD versus a 37% historical average. 81% of large-cap growth funds are outperforming, the highest share in over a decade. Only 4% of large-cap value funds are outperforming, even though value funds have the best absolute YTD return.
Mutual fund cash balances are 1.1% of assets as of the end of September, matching the December 2025 record low. Cash rose briefly around the start of the US-Iran war and then fell back.

Active US equity mutual funds have seen roughly $350B of outflows YTD and are on track for a 12th consecutive year of outflows. US equity ETFs have taken in about $960B YTD and about $210B since the start of Q4. ETF inflows keep GS's Sentiment Indicator positive, while hedge fund equity exposure has declined over the past month.

AI complex: excluding mega-caps, AI-exposed equities were 12% of the average large-cap fund at the start of Q4, a 130 bp underweight. The underweight narrowed from 175 bp during Q3. Including mega-caps, AI-exposed equities were 34% of portfolios versus a 40% benchmark weight. The AI basket has struggled since the start of Q4.

Within AI, funds bought selectively in Q3. The most popular increases included AMD, WDC, STX and SNDK in AI infrastructure and PLTR, SNOW, TWLO, PANW and CRWD in software. AMD, PLTR and SNDK had the three largest net increases in fund ownership across the Russell 3000, despite funds being underweight AMD, PLTR, SNDK and WDC.
The most popular Q3 decreases included semiconductor equipment and networking names AMAT, LRCX, CSCO and KLAC. A majority of funds also trimmed JCI, though funds remain overweight it on average.

Magnificent 7: the average large-cap fund was 722 bp underweight at the end of Q3 2026, effectively unchanged on the quarter. By style the underweight is growth (1,002) bp, core (731) bp and value (434) bp. Part of the underweight comes from diversification restrictions.

The average fund is underweight every Mag 7 name except AMZN, its first average overweight since 2016. Only AAPL and AMZN have beaten the equal-weight S&P 500 YTD, and four Mag 7 names are down YTD. A majority of funds cut ownership of every Mag 7 name except MSFT, with the largest net reductions in GOOGL and AAPL.

Wide return dispersion and improved market breadth have helped active fund returns. Breadth improved through a catch-up by laggards and a modest catch-down by the largest stocks. Dispersion stayed high because higher single-stock volatility offset higher correlations.

Mutual funds were relatively well placed for Q4 volatility. Across the top 15 best and worst S&P 500 performers QTD, the average fund was slightly overweight the median best performer and 3 bp underweight the median worst performer.

Sector positioning: the average fund is most overweight Industrials (+200 bp), Health Care (+199 bp, a 10-year high) and Financials (+196 bp). It is most underweight Info Tech (-631 bp). Industrials, Health Care, Energy and Staples overweights rank at or above the 95th percentile of the past 10 years, while Communication Services and Info Tech tilts sit at the 3rd percentile.

Quarter-on-quarter, funds added most to Info Tech (+29 bp), with the increase concentrated in Software and Semiconductors. They cut most from Financials (-35 bp), led by Banks (-22 bp). JPM, BAC and C were among the 20 most popular decreases. Funds across styles trimmed Consumer Staples and Utilities.

Health Care demand is tied to its inverse correlation with the AI trade during recent AI volatility. Funds added most to Life Sciences Tools, now the second largest overweight in the sector behind Health Care Providers. RVTY, ILMN and TMO were among the most popular increases.

Stock baskets: since the start of Q4 the largest mutual fund overweights basket (GSTHMFOW) returned +5% versus +3% for the equal-weight S&P 500 and -7% for the underweights basket (GSTHMFUW). YTD the underweights basket still leads, 16% versus 8%. Both baskets were rebalanced with 13 new overweight and 7 new underweight constituents.

Largest average fund overweights by style: core is MA, V, DHR and TMO. Growth is AMZN (+298 bp), TMO, STX and INTC. Value is GOOGL (+120 bp), NVDA, TXN and SCHW. Largest underweights are AAPL, NVDA, TSLA, MU and AMD in core, NVDA (-456 bp) and GOOGL (-301 bp) in growth, and AAPL and AMZN in value.

sector_views.rationale: Average large-cap fund is +200 bp overweight, the largest sector overweight, at or above the 95th percentile of the past 10 years. This describes fund positioning, not a GS rating.
Average fund is +199 bp overweight, a 10-year high. Its inverse correlation with the AI trade has lifted its popularity. Fund positioning, not a GS rating.
Average fund is +196 bp overweight but cut the tilt by 35 bp in Q3, the largest sector reduction, led by Banks. Fund positioning, not a GS rating.
Average fund is 631 bp underweight, at the 3rd percentile of 10 years, but lifted its tilt by 29 bp in Q3, led by Software and Semiconductors. Fund positioning, not a GS rating.
Funds across all styles trimmed tilts to both sectors in Q3. Fund positioning, not a GS rating.

macro_indicators.indicator: US equity mutual fund cash balances
macro_indicators.interpretation: Matches the December 2025 record low. Funds are close to fully invested, so there is little cash left to add to equities.

risk_factors: The AI complex has been weak since the start of Q4. Names such as INTC, MRVL, SNDK, LRCX and STX are down 36% to 55% QTD.
Mutual funds remain underweight AI-exposed equities and the Mag 7, so a renewed AI rally would hurt relative performance.
Narrow market breadth would weigh on active fund excess returns. Breadth has improved for now.
Active equity mutual funds face a 12th consecutive year of outflows while passive ETFs absorb flows.
Overweight and underweight tilts can be distorted by stock performance and benchmark weights, which is why GS also looks at shares owned.
charts_described: Exhibit 3 plots US equity mutual fund cash at 1.1% of total assets and $145 billion as of September 30, 2026.
Exhibit 25 shows YTD returns of 8% for GSTHMFOW, 16% for GSTHMFUW, 8% for the S&P 500 and 14% for the equal-weight S&P 500.
Exhibit 9 shows average Mag 7 underweights of (722) bp, with growth (1002) bp, core (731) bp and value (434) bp.
Exhibit 2 gives YTD returns versus benchmarks by style, for example large-cap value 14.4% versus 23.1% and large-cap growth (0.3)% versus (5.9)%.
vol_and_positioning: Active mutual funds are 130 bp underweight AI-exposed equities ex mega-caps, down from 175 bp at the end of Q2, and 722 bp underweight the Mag 7.
Mutual fund cash at 1.1% of assets matches the record low.
Hedge fund equity exposure has declined over the past month while ETF inflows keep GS's Sentiment Indicator in positive territory.
Average mutual fund tilts: Health Care at a 10-year high, Communication Services and Info Tech at the 3rd percentile of the past 10 years.
Net fund buyers in Q3 were led by AMD (+57 funds net), PLTR (+46) and SNDK (+45). Net sellers were led by GOOGL (-127), JNJ (-108) and AVGO (-105).
Return dispersion remains elevated and S&P 500 52-week breadth has improved sharply. GS's regression shows dispersion and breadth are major drivers of mutual fund excess returns.
geopolitical: Mutual fund cash balances rose briefly around the start of the US-Iran war before falling back to 1.1% of assets.

theme_stances.key_argument: Despite their underweight to AI-exposed stocks overall, mutual funds added exposure to select pockets of the AI complex in Q3.
theme_stances.evidence: Mutual funds remain selective within the AI complex

theme_stances.theme: dispersion and breadth helping active funds
theme_stances.key_argument: Mutual funds typically deliver the best excess returns when return dispersion is wide and market breadth is not narrow.
theme_stances.evidence: High return dispersion and an improvement in market breadth have supported mutual fund performance.

theme_stances.key_argument: Health Care's inverse correlation with the AI trade lifted the sector's popularity amid recent AI volatility.
theme_stances.evidence: Mutual funds have lifted tilts to Health Care to a new 10-year high.
